title: Traumatic brain injury and concussion in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the head injury (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Fall from a ladder resulting in a head injury.

Review of Systems:
The patient reports headache and mild dizziness. He denies any focal weakness, numbness, vision changes, or difficulty speaking. He denies any changes in gait or balance. He reports no nausea or vomiting.

Social History:
The patient is a retired carpenter who lives at home with his wife. He is a former smoker but quit twenty years ago. He reports no history of illicit substance use.

Family History:
Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes. Siblings are all living and healthy.

Vitals:
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 78 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air

Recent Labs:
Hemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 8.5 x 10^9/L
Platelets: 210 x 10^9/L
Sodium: 139 mEq/L
Potassium: 4.1 mEq/L
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2

Hospital Course:
The patient is an 86-year-old male admitted following a fall from a ladder. He presented to the emergency department with complaints of a headache. He did not lose consciousness at any time during the incident. Initial imaging and neurological examinations were performed. An MRI of the head revealed a diffuse brain injury. The patient was admitted for observation and management of his symptoms. During his stay, he remained stable and showed no signs of neurological decline. He was monitored for cognitive changes and motor function. He participated in physical therapy to address balance and safety. He was cleared for discharge once his symptoms were stable and he demonstrated safe mobility.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Diffuse brain injury
2. Fall from ladder

Discharge Medications:
1. Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for pain.
2. Meloxicam 7.5mg daily.

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with his primary care physician in one week for a routine checkup and to discuss his rehabilitation plan. He was instructed to seek immediate medical attention if he experiences worsening headaches or confusion.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
05/18/2026
explanations: Diffuse traumatic brain injury without loss of consciousness, initial encounter: S06.2X0A (HCC 399).

distractors.why: No loss of consciousness is documented.

hccs.label: Major Head Injury without Loss of Consciousness
